documents.content:
# Employee eligibility and new-hire coverage

Regular employees scheduled for at least 20 hours per week are eligible for benefits.
Contractors and temporary employees are not eligible under this policy.
New hires must complete a 60-day waiting period.
Coverage starts on the first day of the month following completion of the waiting period.
New hires may submit enrollment selections during the waiting period using the Benefits > Enrollment page.
The annual enrollment closing date does not cancel a new hire's enrollment opportunity.
documents.title: Employee eligibility and new-hire coverage

documents.content:
# Commuter transit reimbursement

Commuter reimbursement is limited to $120 per employee per calendar month.
Eligible expenses are public-transit passes used for travel between home and work.
Parking fees, fuel, and gym memberships are not eligible commuter expenses.
Submit a paid transit receipt within 60 calendar days of purchase.
Unused monthly commuter allowance does not carry forward.
Commuter and wellness reimbursements have separate limits and receipt deadlines.
documents.title: Commuter transit reimbursement

documents.content:
# Wellness reimbursement policy for 2026

Wellness reimbursement is limited to $300 per employee per calendar year.
Eligible expenses include gym memberships and instructor-led fitness classes.
Home exercise equipment, nutritional supplements, and commuting expenses are not eligible.
Submit a paid, itemized receipt within 90 calendar days of the purchase date.
Unused wellness allowance does not carry forward.
This current policy replaces the archived 2025 wellness policy and its lower reimbursement cap.
documents.title: Wellness reimbursement policy for 2026

documents.content:
# Medical plan deductible and out-of-pocket limit

The medical plan has a $1,500 individual annual deductible for in-network care.
The individual annual in-network out-of-pocket limit is $4,500.
These amounts apply to medical benefits only. The dental annual maximum is a separate limit.
The knowledge base does not list procedure-specific medical coverage, individual premiums, or out-of-network reimbursement amounts.
documents.title: Medical plan deductible and out-of-pocket limit

documents.content:
# Benefits support and urgent coverage escalation

Open a support request through Benefits > Help and include the claim reference when relevant.
If a claim remains In review for more than five business days, request a status escalation through Benefits > Help.
For an urgent loss-of-coverage concern, choose Priority: Urgent coverage.
The benefits support team aims to acknowledge urgent coverage requests within one business day.
This acknowledgement target is not a claim payment guarantee or a promise that an appeal will be approved.
documents.title: Benefits support and urgent coverage escalation

documents.content:
# Dental annual maximum and preventive care

The dental plan pays up to $1,500 per covered person per calendar year.
Preventive dental exams and cleanings have no deductible.
The dental annual maximum is separate from the medical deductible and medical out-of-pocket limit.
Unused dental benefits do not carry forward into the next calendar year.
documents.title: Dental annual maximum and preventive care
